title: David B. Wilkins on Declining Black HLS Enrollment
author: David B. Wilkins

dom.t: Legal workforce: Junior pipelines face the sharpest risk

mo.t: Career inequality: Professional change preserves unequal rewards
Legal workforce: Junior pipelines face the sharpest risk

kp.k: Black first-year enrollment at Harvard Law declined sharply
kp.d: The CLP news item quotes the New York Times reporting that Harvard Law enrolled 19 first-year Black students, representing 3.4 percent of the class and the lowest number since the 1960s, citing American Bar Association data. The Times's analysis put the previous year's figure at 43. The item is dated December 12, 2025, but links to a Times article with a December 16, 2024 URL; the enrollment comparison is expressed as “Last year” rather than explicit academic years. This is evidence about legal education demographics, not AI's effects.
qs: Harvard Law enrolled 19 first-year Black students, or 3.4 percent of the class, the lowest number since the 1960s, according to the data from the American Bar Association.
Last year, the law school’s first-year class had 43 Black students, according to an analysis by The New York Times.

kp.k: Wilkins attributes a role to the Supreme Court decision
kp.d: Wilkins told the Times that the Supreme Court decision and Harvard College's being named in the case played a role in the enrollment decline. This is Wilkins's attributed explanation; the brief item supplies no causal analysis or estimate of either factor's contribution.

pts.k: The source makes no substantive AI claim. In its own domain, Wilkins attributes part of the decline in Black Harvard Law School enrollment to the Supreme Court decision and Harvard College's involvement in the case.
pts.d: Wilkins offers a qualified causal explanation, saying these factors played a role rather than claiming they were the sole cause. The accompanying enrollment figures are reporting attributed to the New York Times, not findings attributed to Wilkins. The ChatGPT item appears only as a related-content title.

pts.k: The source supplies enrollment statistics documenting the decline, but no empirical causal analysis supporting Wilkins's explanation.
pts.d: The quoted New York Times reporting cites American Bar Association data for 19 Black first-year students, representing 3.4 percent of the class, and a Times analysis for the preceding year's count of 43. Wilkins's involvement in surveys of Black HLS alumni provides experiential context; no survey findings are presented as evidence for the causal claim.

The excerpt compares recently released figures with 'Last year' without explicitly identifying the entering cohorts, so those relative dates should not be resolved solely from the page date.
